title: Hook kind: post-comment
description: Posts a comment on the issue or PR using a template file. The template is rendered with the lifecycle event's context (issue.number, issue.title, repo, etc.) and posted via `gh issue comment` or `gh pr comment`. Per DEC-024. Idempotent per firing: the comment's first line is the stamp `<!-- pkit-hook: <stamp_id>:<firing> -->`, where `<firing>` is a digest of the stamp_id, the lifecycle event, the issue or PR, on `after_move_issue` the transition's from and to states and the issue's count of landed moves, and on `after_close_issue` the time the issue was closed. A retry of the same firing posts nothing; a transition the issue makes again, or a close after a reopen, posts its own comment. Where the count or the close time cannot be read, the firing is told without it. The engine skips only when a comment opening with that line was posted, and not edited since, by the account `gh` posts as; a comment by anyone else, or an edited one, never stops a post. When the comments cannot be read, the engine posts and warns.

template_path.description: Path to the template, relative to the capability root (e.g., `project/hook-templates/close-comment.md`). Must live under `project/` (adopter-owned per the no-shared-files invariant). The template renders with mustache-style placeholders: `{{ issue.number }}`, `{{ issue.title }}`, `{{ repo }}`, etc.

stamp_id.description: Optional stable identifier for the comment's idempotency stamp. Defaults to the template_path's basename without extension. The engine writes `<!-- pkit-hook: <stamp_id>:<firing> -->` as the first line of the rendered comment, showing the id as lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens (at most 64 characters), and detects a retry of the same firing by that line on a comment the posting account wrote and nobody edited.
